subject: Unexpected September spike — duplicate session counts & EU VAT credit request
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen@streamline.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Sudden usage spike on invoice — immediate breakdown requested

Hi Soojin,

We just received our September invoice and there’s a ~3.6x jump in billed tokens vs. our historical baseline for the same workload. I’ve attached a short CSV (stream_usage_summary.csv) showing the hourly count from our side and the invoice line references.

This spike looks like it began on 2027-09-04 02:00 UTC and persisted for roughly 18 hours. Our engineering team hasn’t rolled any changes in that window. Can you: 
- Provide a per-request breakdown (timestamps, model, token counts) for the affected window
- Flag any duplicate session IDs or repeated request IDs you see
- Let us know next steps for withholding payment until we resolve this — we are an EU entity; VAT handling and any provisional credit are important for our accounting close.

We’re attaching the usage CSV and our billing contact (billing@streamline.ai).\n
Thanks,
Ellen Park
Head of Revenue Ops
Streamline.ai
Attachments: stream_usage_summary.csv

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@streamline.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 11:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden usage spike on invoice — immediate breakdown requested

Hi Ellen — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the CSV. I’m escalating this to our billing team and engineering to get a fast root-cause breakdown.

Quick notes:
- I’ve asked Priyom to pull raw request logs and sampling traces for 2027-09-04 00:00–12:00 UTC.
- Markus, can we provisionally place invoice INV-2027-09-04 (Streamline.ai) on hold pending the investigation? If so, what is the earliest we can confirm a temporary credit to avoid payment penalties?

Ellen: can you confirm whether you were running any test harnesses or load generators from behind a shared NAT/proxy during the window? Also send your EU VAT ID if you’d like the adjustment reflected on the proforma.

I’ll follow up by EOD with the next steps.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ellen Park <ellen@streamline.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 15:28:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden usage spike on invoice — initial log analysis attached

Hi all,

I pulled the raw traces for the window Ellen flagged and ran a quick de-dup sampling. Attached are two artifacts: ingest_logs_snippet.txt (five representative request groups) and sampling_report.pdf (summary of dedup/shard counts).

Findings (initial):
- We observed a cluster of request groups between 2027-09-04 02:04–02:28 UTC where session_id values repeat across multiple request lines but with differing request_id suffixes. This pattern typically indicates client-side retries where the client re-sends at the application layer but the session identifier is unchanged.
- In roughly 42% of the repeated groups the token count is recorded twice — once for the original call and again for the retry, because the client did not use idempotent request semantics and our ingestion dedupe window was too narrow for the heavy retry burst.
- We also saw a small number (~6%) of requests from the same public IP that map to different internal tenant identifiers — looks like a CI runner using ephemeral API keys was reusing sessions across jobs, which inflated your billed sessions.

Next steps I recommend: 
1) We can reprocess the affected window with a widened dedup window and apply de-duplication heuristics to recompute billable tokens.
2) If reprocessing shows confirmed duplicate token counts, Redwood proposes a provisional credit of the duplicated tokens (we’ll compute exact tokencount and EUR amount).
3) We’ll produce an anonymized evidence pack (sampling_report.pdf + logs snippet) for your auditors and mark the invoice status to "on hold" until we complete the reprocessing.

I’ve started the reprocess job; ETA ~24–36 hours. Ellen — please confirm whether your CI/runner teams want us to exclude certain API keys from reprocessing to avoid removing legitimate bursts.

Attachments: ingest_logs_snippet.txt, sampling_report.pdf

On Mon, 6 Sep 2027 at 11:04, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Ellen — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the CSV. I’m escalating this to our billing team and engineering to get a fast root-cause breakdown.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Billing Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Ellen Park <ellen@streamline.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: billing@streamline.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 08:09:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden usage spike on invoice — duplicate session counts & EU VAT credit request

Thanks Priyom — that matches what our engineers suspected (we had a batch of CI pipelines that re-ran during the overnight deploy window).

Confirming:
- Please exclude API keys prefixed with "ci-" from de-duplication; those are legitimate CI runs and should remain billed.
- Please de-dupe any requests where the session_id is identical and request timestamps are within 5 minutes and request paths/params match (we accept those as accidental retries).
- Our EU VAT ID: GB999888777. Please include it in the proforma if you can reflect the provisional credit.

We need an interim credit note for accounting — can you provide a provisional proforma credit PDF we can route to our finance team? Once we see the proforma we can confirm whether to hold payment for INV-2027-09-04.

Ellen Park
Head of Revenue Ops
Streamline.ai

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@streamline.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 18:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden usage spike on invoice — provisional credit & invoice hold

Hi Ellen — following Priyom's initial reprocess summary we completed an expedited recompute and generated a provisional credit. Key points:

- Recompute window: 2027-09-04 00:00–12:00 UTC.
- Dedupe rule applied: identical session_id + matching path + timestamps within 5 minutes = mark retry; duplicates removed.
- Result: 1,872,640 duplicated tokens identified, provisional credit EUR 3,745.28 (converted at rate used in invoice).
- We’ve created a provisional proforma: proforma_credit_note.pdf (attached) and updated invoice INV-2027-09-04 status to ON_HOLD in our billing system.

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm receipt of the proforma and your VAT ID (we have GB999888777).
2) If confirmed, we’ll issue a formal credit memo within 5 business days and update the finalized invoice.
3) DocuSign link below for standard credit memo acknowledgment (necessary for audit trails): https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/placeholder/Envelope12345

Ellen — once you sign the DocuSign acknowledgment and confirm the VAT ID, we’ll mark the invoice as adjusted and notify your accounting team and our collections team to stop any dunning.

Thanks for the quick coordination.

Best regards,
Markus Klein
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: proforma_credit_note.pdf
